title: When Parents Look at Their Screens

paragraphs.english: With so much focus on children’s use of screens, it’s easy for parents to forget about their own screen use. “Tech is designed to really suck you in,” says Jenny Radesky in her study of digital play, “and digital products are there to promote maximal engagement. It makes it hard to disengage, and leads to a lot of bleed-over into the family routine.”
paragraphs.chinese: 人们如此关注孩子使用屏幕的问题，家长反倒很容易忘记自己怎样使用屏幕。珍妮·拉德斯基在有关数字游戏的研究中说：“科技产品的设计就是要把你牢牢吸引住，数字产品追求的是最大程度的参与。这让人很难抽离，也使它们大量渗入家庭的日常生活。”

paragraphs.english: Radesky has studied the use of mobile phones and tablets at mealtimes by giving mother-child pairs a food-testing exercise. She found that mothers who used devices during the exercise started 20 per cent fewer verbal and 39 per cent fewer nonverbal interactions with their children. During a separate observation, she saw that phones became a source of tension in the family. Parents would be looking at their emails while the children would be making excited bids for their attention.
paragraphs.chinese: 拉德斯基通过让母亲与孩子成对参加食物试吃活动，研究了用餐时使用手机和平板电脑的情况。她发现，在活动中使用设备的母亲，与孩子主动发起的语言交流少了百分之二十，非语言互动少了百分之三十九。在另一次观察中，她发现手机成了家庭紧张关系的来源：父母可能在看邮件，孩子却正兴奋地努力吸引他们的注意。

paragraphs.english: Infants are wired to look at parents’ faces to try to understand their world, and if those faces are blank and unresponsive — as they often are when absorbed in a device — it can be extremely disconcerting for the children. Radesky cites the “still face experiment” devised by developmental psychologist Ed Tronick in the 1970s. In it, a mother is asked to interact with her child in a normal way before putting on a blank expression and not giving them any visual social feedback: The child becomes increasingly distressed as she tries to capture her mother’s attention. “Parents don’t have to be exquisitely present at all times, but there needs to be a balance and parents need to be responsive and sensitive to a child’s verbal or nonverbal expressions of an emotional need,” says Radesky.
paragraphs.chinese: 婴儿天生会注视父母的脸，以此尝试理解周围的世界；如果父母的脸毫无表情、没有回应——沉迷设备时往往就是如此——孩子会感到十分不安。拉德斯基援引了发展心理学家埃德·特罗尼克在二十世纪七十年代设计的“静止脸实验”。实验先要求母亲正常地与孩子互动，然后面无表情，不再给予任何可见的社交反馈；孩子一边尝试引起母亲注意，一边越来越痛苦。拉德斯基说：“父母不必时刻全神贯注地陪伴，但必须有所平衡，并且应当对孩子通过语言或非语言方式表达的情感需求保持敏感，及时回应。”

paragraphs.english: On the other hand, Tronick himself is concerned that the worries about kids’ use of screens are born out of an “oppressive ideology that demands that parents should always be interacting” with their children: “It’s based on a somewhat fantasised, very white, very upper-middle-class ideology that says if you’re failing to expose your child to 30,000 words you are neglecting them.” Tronick believes that just because a child isn’t learning from the screen doesn’t mean there’s no value to it — particularly if it gives parents time to have a shower, do housework or simply have a break from their child. Parents, he says, can get a lot out of using their devices to speak to a friend or get some work out of the way. This can make them feel happier, which lets them be more available to their child the rest of the time.
paragraphs.chinese: 另一方面，特罗尼克本人担心，人们对孩子使用屏幕的忧虑，源于一种“压迫性的观念”，要求父母应当始终与孩子互动。他说：“这种观念多少有些不切实际，带着十分明显的白人中上阶层色彩；它认为，如果你没有让孩子接触三万个词，就是疏于照顾。”特罗尼克认为，孩子没有从屏幕里学到东西，并不意味着屏幕毫无价值，尤其是当它能让父母抽时间洗澡、做家务，或只是暂时从照看孩子中休息一下。他说，父母利用设备与朋友交流，或处理掉一些工作，也能获益很多。这会让他们心情更好，从而在其余时间更有余力陪伴孩子。

sentenceNotes.sentence: Infants are wired to look at parents’ faces to try to understand their world, and if those faces are blank and unresponsive — as they often are when absorbed in a device — it can be extremely disconcerting for the children.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: Infants are wired to look at parents’ faces, and it can be disconcerting for the children.
sentenceNotes.structure: and 连接两个分句；第二个分句前有 if 条件从句；破折号内 as 从句补充说明父母沉迷设备时的常见表现，when absorbed 省略了主语和 be。
sentenceNotes.translation: 婴儿天生会看父母的脸来理解世界，如果父母的脸毫无表情、没有回应——沉迷设备时常会如此——孩子就可能非常不安。
sentenceNotes.tip: those faces 回指父母的脸；be wired to 表示天生倾向，并非字面“接上线”。

sentenceNotes.sentence: Tronick believes that just because a child isn’t learning from the screen doesn’t mean there’s no value to it — particularly if it gives parents time to have a shower, do housework or simply have a break from their child.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: Tronick believes that one fact doesn’t mean there’s no value to the screen.
sentenceNotes.structure: believes 后为 that 宾语从句；其中 just because ... doesn’t mean ... 表示“不能仅因……就认为……”；if 从句强调对父母产生价值的条件；have a shower、do housework、have a break 并列。
sentenceNotes.translation: 特罗尼克认为，不能仅因为孩子没有从屏幕中学习，就认定它没有价值，尤其是它让父母有时间洗澡、做家务或暂时休息一下时。
sentenceNotes.tip: 双重否定并未断言屏幕必有教育价值，作者强调的可能是给父母带来的帮助。
